# Configuration keys

Source: `config/harness-knobs.json`.

## Host lane settings

Set these in `[domains.lanes]` in the host configuration. Omit a key for its default.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `user_skills` | discover | Discover host user skills for lanes read-only. off disables host user skill discovery unless overridden by domains.lanes.projects.{project_id}.user_skills or route policy lane.user_skills. Route policy wins over project, then host. Inspect value, default and origin with config show or config schema. (discover or off). |
| `skill_stage_max_bytes` | 16777216 | Maximum bytes copied into an attempt's read-only user skill tree. Content exceeding the bound is skipped with a warning. Inspect value and origin with config show. (bytes, 0 or more). |
| `projects.{project}.capabilities` | empty | Capabilities granted by default to this project's writer lanes; node settings and invocation flags may override them. Read-only lanes do not inherit them. (postgres). |
| `projects.{project}.shared_paths` | empty | Existing paths shared read-write with this project's writers. Absolute, ~/ and primary-checkout-relative paths are accepted. Git, credential, protected and executable paths are omitted with a warning. Read-only lanes receive no additional writes. (existing absolute, ~/ or checkout-relative paths). |
| `projects.{project}.exec_roots` | empty | Read-and-execute directory subtrees relative to the primary checkout. Entries escaping that checkout, missing, protected, credential or writable targets are ignored with a warning naming the configuration key. (directory paths relative to the primary checkout). |

## Host lane build settings

Set these in `[domains.fabric.lanes]` in the host configuration. Omit a key for its host-dependent default; -1 also selects automatic behaviour.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `start_spacing_ms` | 0 | Milliseconds between starts of the same lane class, for both writers and read-only lanes. Build slots gate heavy runs independently. (0 to 600000). |
| `memory_pressure_threshold` | critical | Kernel memory pressure level at which new lanes wait on macOS. warning also defers at critical; never disables the pressure gate. The disk floor still applies; the memory floor is advisory. (critical, warning or never). |
| `max_concurrent_builds` | max(1, min(cores / cargo_build_jobs, GiB of RAM / 6)) | A build throttle, not a hard cap: cargo builds, tests, checks and lints that a lane's cargo shim runs at once across the host and every project that shares the state directory. Lanes are not capped by it; a command that compiles waits for a free slot. Direct ~/.cargo/bin/cargo, rustc and non-cargo builds are not gated. (1 to 64 or -1 for auto). |
| `build_wait_minutes` | 30 | Minutes a build waits for a build slot or another build's Cargo lock before it gives up with an error. (1 to 1440 or -1 for auto). |
| `lane_port_base` | 30000 | First port of the range split into per-writer-lane blocks. A writer with an allocated block holds it for its lifetime and sees PROVENANT_LANE_PORT_BASE and PROVENANT_LANE_PORT_COUNT. Unreadable lane-port settings or allocation I/O errors warn and skip allocation. (1024 to 65535 or -1 for auto). |
| `lane_port_block` | 16 | Ports in each writer lane's block (PROVENANT_LANE_PORT_COUNT). (1 to 1024 or -1 for auto). |
| `lane_port_blocks` | 64 | Blocks in the range, so the most writer lanes that hold a block at once; the base plus blocks times block size must be at most 65536. 0 turns allocation off. A writer launched while every block is held is not started and reports no free port block. (0 to 1024 or -1 for auto). |
| `max_lanes` | unset (no limit) | Most lanes of any class live at once across the host; a lane beyond it queues and is refused with the limit and source. (1 to 64 or -1 for auto). |
| `max_project_lanes` | unset (no limit) | Most lanes of any class live at once for one project; at most max_lanes. (1 to 32 or -1 for auto). |
| `max_writer_lanes` | unset (no limit) | Most writer lanes live at once across the host; a writer beyond it queues and is then refused with a reason naming the cap. (1 to 64 or -1 for auto). |
| `max_project_writer_lanes` | unset (no limit) | Most writer lanes live at once for one project; at most max_writer_lanes. (1 to 32 or -1 for auto). |
| `cargo_build_jobs` | Half the available cores, at least 1 | Default CARGO_BUILD_JOBS for lanes; an inherited value takes precedence. (1 to 1024 or -1 for auto). |
| `cargo_incremental` | false | CARGO_INCREMENTAL for lanes. Incremental sessions grow a lane's target without bound and are rarely reused; a value already in the lane environment takes precedence. (true or false). |
| `cargo_debug` | line-tables-only | CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG for lanes. Line tables keep backtraces at a fraction of the size of full debug information; a value already in the lane environment takes precedence. (none, line-directives-only, line-tables-only, limited, full, 0, 1, 2, true or false). |
| `build_dir_max_bytes` | 21474836480 (20 GiB) | Cap on the allocated bytes of all Cargo profile directories in lane caches, idle and busy alike. Collection removes idle directories, least recently used first, during manual or scheduled GC, when admission finds the disk below gc.free_floor, and in `provenant gc`; a directory whose Cargo locks are held is never removed. When busy directories alone exceed the cap, every eligible idle directory is removed and the total stays over. (bytes, 0 or more). |
| `build_dir_grace_seconds` | 900 (15 minutes) | A profile directory whose newest file or directory modification is within this many seconds is never removed, even when its Cargo locks are free: test and run binaries execute after Cargo drops its locks, and Cargo may be opening its lock files. Zero removes the protection. It protects only recently written directories: a test or run binary that runs longer than the grace without writing under target/ is unprotected unless a Cargo lock is still held. (seconds, 0 or more). |
| `build_dir_survey_interval_seconds` | 300 (5 minutes) | Legacy survey interval, retained for readable existing configurations. Settlement no longer surveys lane caches; manual and scheduled GC own those surveys. (seconds, 0 or more). |

## Host run settings

Set these in `[domains.run]` in the host configuration. Omit a key for its default.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `profile_limit_bytes` | 524288 | Maximum rendered macOS sandbox profile size. Increase for lanes with many grants; profiles pass through argv and may still hit OS limits. (1 or more bytes). |
| `writer_token_budget` | 500000 | Tokens a writer attempt may use, from the fresh usage its provider reports, before it is ended so a continuation can pick it up. The host then attempts to commit and publish the lane's work; it does not when custody is not absent, when a merge, cherry-pick, revert or rebase is in progress, or when the commit fails, and settlement notes say which. 0 turns the budget off. Cache reads do not count. Enforced for Claude from live usage and for Codex at completed-turn boundaries. Codex reports usage in turn.completed frames, so the host can stop it after a turn passes the budget but cannot interrupt a turn mid-flight. Other providers without live usage are not enforced. Launch warnings or receipt notes say so. Current lane adapters cannot receive a live steer: the 90% warning records an unsupported control receipt. After custody is absent the host attempts a bounded commit only when no Git operation is in progress; an in-progress merge is preserved for stopped-merge handling, a cherry-pick, revert or rebase in progress is left uncommitted, and a skipped or failed commit is reported without replacing the budget outcome. Time queued for a build slot does not count towards the wall-clock deadline, up to lanes.slot_wait_seconds in total. The source (run, project, host or default) is shown with the budget. (0 or more tokens). |
| `projects.{project}.writer_token_budget` | host writer_token_budget | Replace the host writer token budget for this project. (0 or more tokens). |
| `grant_limit` | 128 | Maximum total plan roots and entries in each provider profile family; authentication and native-control families retain minimum caps of 16 and 64. Increase for lanes needing more roots. (1 or more). |
| `write_grant_limit_bytes` | 262144 | Maximum encoded bytes of applied write grants recorded for a lane. Increase when an otherwise valid grant ledger exceeds the default; terminal records retain bounded headroom. (1 to 8388608 bytes). |
| `argv_prompt_limit_bytes` | 65536 | Maximum prompt bytes passed directly to argv adapters. Larger top-level prompts spill to an attempt-owned file; nested attempts refuse rather than use a parent-writable spill. The overall 1 MiB prompt bound and operating-system argument limits still apply. (1 or more bytes). |
| `continuation_copy_limit_bytes` | 4294967296 | Maximum retained provider state bytes copied into a continuation. Available disk space may lower the effective copy budget. Refusals report the setting and source; raise it or reduce state before retrying. (1 or more bytes). |
| `continuation_copy_entries` | 100000 | Maximum entries searched or copied from retained provider state for a continuation. Refusals report the setting and source; raise it or reduce state before retrying. (1 to 4294967295 entries). |
| `continuation_copy_depth` | 32 | Maximum directory depth searched or copied from retained provider state for a continuation. Raising it does not relax credential, hard-link, filesystem or worktree-overlap guards. (1 to 4294967295 directories). |
| `source_view_seconds` | 300 | Total time allowed to build the pinned source view of a `--use review` lane. The view is built with one batched object read, so a healthy large repository needs far less. Raise it on a slow disk or a heavily loaded host. (1 or more seconds). |
| `source_view_entries` | 100000 | Maximum files in a pinned source view. A larger tree is refused, naming this limit. (1 to 4294967295 files). |
| `source_view_bytes` | 536870912 | Maximum total file bytes in a pinned source view. A larger tree is refused, naming this limit. (1 or more bytes). |
| `writer_writes` | [] | Directories writer lanes may read, write and execute as subtrees; read-only lanes are unchanged (up to 16 absolute, safe directory paths outside credential roots). |
| `review_exempt` | ["docs/release-notes/next.d/", "docs/specs/", "Cargo.lock", ".tracker-input"] | Paths that do not count toward an uncommitted outcome; a project list replaces the host list and an empty list disables exemptions (repository-relative paths without wildcards). |
| `push_conflict_markers` | true | Refuse pushes that add lines starting with <<<<<<< or >>>>>>> (true or false). |
| `projects.{project}.writer_writes` | host writer_writes | Replace the host writer_writes list for this project; an empty list grants no host-configured writer roots. Origin: host configuration [domains.run.projects.<project ID>]. (up to 16 absolute, safe directory paths outside credential roots). |

| `approval_tier` | auto | What approval a pull request needs. none: CI only. carry: a review that still covers the head, a change after it that touches only tests, docs or review-exempt paths, or a review of the delta since. delta: as carry, but every change after the review needs its own review. auto is none for a pull request that touches only tests, docs or review-exempt paths, and carry otherwise. ## Host graph settings

Set these in `[domains.fabric.graph]` in the host configuration. Omit a key for its default.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `ci_poll_backoff.initial_seconds` | 0 | Initial delay after a pending CI observation. Each later observation doubles the delay up to max_seconds; the remaining CI timeout takes precedence. Zero makes the gate eligible at the next tick. (seconds, 0 or more). |
| `ci_poll_backoff.max_seconds` | 0 | Maximum per-gate polling delay. The 60-second scheduler interval determines the earliest automatic re-check. (seconds, 0 or more). |
| `ci_poll_overrides.<node_id>` | empty | Override the host CI polling policy for one node ID. Values and origins appear in config show. (initial_seconds and max_seconds). |
| `allowed_read_roots` | empty (read roots stay inside the project and its registered worktrees) | Absolute host directories that template `read_roots` may name besides the project's own registered worktrees. (absolute directory paths). |
| `limits.expansion_depth` | 64 | Longest dependency chain in edges, root nodes at depth 0, and deepest composite nesting a graph may expand to. Graph documents cannot raise it. (1 or more). |
| `limits.continuations` | 2 | Graph continuations limit. (0 or more). |
| `limits.nodes` | 512 | Graph nodes limit. (1 or more). |
| `limits.edges` | 4096 | Graph edges limit. (1 or more). |
| `limits.routes_per_node` | 16 | Graph routes per node limit. (1 or more). |
| `limits.review_substitutions` | 1 | Maximum substitutions per review member. (0 or more). |
| `limits.node_prompt_bytes` | 262144 | Graph node prompt bytes limit. (1 or more). |
| `limits.graph_prompt_bytes` | 4194304 | Graph graph prompt bytes limit. (1 or more). |
| `limits.fan_out_width` | 32 | Graph fan out width limit. (1 or more). |
| `limits.concurrency` | 0 | Graph concurrency limit. Zero uses host lane caps. (0 or more). |

## Host GC settings

Set these in `[gc]` in the host configuration. Omit a key for its default.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `graph_checkpoint_days` | 90 | Retain terminal graph checkpoints for at least this many days after their last save (1 to 3650 days). |
| `schedule` | true | Run the daily scheduled sweep. false also skips admission collection; completion cleanup and landing cleanup still run (true or false). |
| `idle_days` | 7 | Minimum idle age before a lane cache or declared output is collected (1 to 3650 days). |
| `free_floor` | 10% of the state volume, at least 50 GiB | Free-space floor for admission, build pauses and pressure collection; below it GC removes further eligible caches oldest first (whole B, K, M, G, T or KiB to TiB; a plain number means GiB). |
| `lane_cargo_cache_max` | 32G | Cap all marked lane Cargo caches; evict oldest eligible caches first while retaining live, foreign and unobserved custody (same syntax as free_floor). |
| `alert_below` | free_floor | Free space below which an applied collection emits one gc.low_disk note per dip (same syntax as free_floor). |
| `projects.{project}.regenerable` | ["target"] with a root Cargo.toml, otherwise [] | Git-ignored directory names collected at any depth in the project's linked worktrees; `.provenant/scratch` is collected in addition without a declaration (directory names; not .git, .worktrees, absolute or parent paths). |
| `projects.{project}.keep` | [] | Paths, their descendants and any matching directory containing them that collection preserves (worktree-relative paths). |
| `projects.{project}.foreign_worktrees` | keep | merged-clean removes clean, merged linked worktrees with no known writer after a complete free census (keep or merged-clean). |

## Host retention settings

Set these in `[retention]` in the host configuration. Omit a key for its default.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `provider_state_days` | 7 | Days a terminal attempt's provider state stays resumable; reread on each sweep (1 to 3650 days). |
| `logs_days` | 30 | Days before captures over 64 KiB and intermediate event rows of closed runs expire; the last 64 KiB is kept as a .tail file (1 to 3650 days). |
| `session_revisions` | 8 | Checkpoint revisions a session keeps, the current one included; reread on each save (1 to 64). |
| `chair_log_days` | 30 | Days a chair log payload is kept (1 to 3650 days). |
| `chair_log_entries` | 10000 | Chair log entries kept per session (1 to 100000). |
| `chair_log_bytes` | 16777216 (16 MiB) | Chair log payload bytes kept per session (65536 to 1073741824 bytes). |
| `chair_log_replay_days` | chair_log_days, at least 7 | Days chair log replay receipts are kept (7 to 3650 days). |
| `projects.{project}.checkpoint_soft_bytes` | 2048 | Advisory checkpoint size above which a save warns; the hard limit is unchanged (1 to 262144 bytes). |

## Host quota settings

Set these in `[domains.quota]` in the host configuration. Omit a key for its default.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `max_parallel` | 3 | Accounts per quota probe batch; batches and probes currently run sequentially. Out-of-range values refuse the file (1 to 16). |
| `wall_budget_seconds` | 55 | Wall-clock budget for a whole quota tick. Out-of-range values refuse the file (1 to 600 seconds). |

## Host OpenCode Go settings

Set these in `[domains.routing.opencode_go]` in the host configuration. Omit a key for its default.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `min_monthly_allowance_usd` | 60 | Lowest documented monthly allowance an OpenCode Go model needs to be routed or selected; a model with an unknown allowance is refused while the floor is on (0 or more; 0 disables the floor). |

## Host Codex cloud settings

Set these in `[providers.codex.cloud]` in the host configuration. Omit a key for its default.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `transport` | official | official uses codex cloud exec, status and list; thread uses a client for the cloud thread API (official or thread). |
| `command` | codex for official, codex-cloud-task for thread | Cloud client executable, resolved through the host PATH (one executable name or path; no arguments). |

## Host store settings

Set these in `[domains.fabric.limits]` in the host configuration. Omit a key for its default.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `store_busy_timeout_ms` | 30000 (30 seconds) | Milliseconds a command waits for a contended local store, both the SQLite busy timeout and the stores' own advisory locks, before it reports contention. Read once when a command starts; zero fails fast (0 to 600000). |

## Host review settings

Set these in `[domains.routing.review]` in the host configuration. Omit a key for its default.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `diversity` | advisory | How a review panel that cannot meet its `minimum_family_counts` is handled. advisory resolves the panel and records one warning per short family, with the required and met counts and the exclusions, in the review-family resolution and each reviewer's preamble; strict refuses the review instead. A run document's `[review]` table can set `diversity` for one review. A lens's own `required_family` always refuses when unmet. (advisory or strict). |

## Host review lens settings

Set these in `[domains.routing.review.lenses.by_paths]` in the host configuration. Omit the table for the bundled rules.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `"<glob>".add` | bundled test-path rules (`**/tests/**`, `**/*.test.*`, `**/conftest.py` and others) add `tests` | Add these review lenses, outside the slot cap and once, when a changed path matches the glob. The reason is recorded as `by_paths:<glob>` in `--explain` and the review report. Setting any `by_paths` table replaces the bundled rules; an empty `[domains.routing.review.lenses.by_paths]` removes them. (lens names, such as tests). |

## Host model policy settings

Set these in `[domains.routing.model_policy]` in the host configuration. Omit a key for its bundled or empty default. `rules.policy` takes the same fields as `defaults`.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `bundled` | true | Start from the bundled per-model policy (cache prices, compaction windows, lane guidance, result checks). false starts empty. (true or false). |
| `defaults.cache.read_share_target` | unset (bundled 0.9) | Advisory cache-read share a lane should reach; reported in stats, never enforced. (0 to 1). |
| `defaults.cache.price_multiplier` | 1.0 (bundled: 2.0 in DeepSeek weekday peak) | Current price multiplier; divides the read-heavy preference weight. (number above 0). |
| `defaults.cache.read_ratio` | per model | Cache-read price divided by uncached input price. (0 or more). |
| `defaults.cache.write_ratio` | per model | Cache-write price divided by uncached input price. (0 or more). |
| `defaults.cache.output_ratio` | per model | Output price divided by uncached input price, for compaction break-even guidance. (0 or more). |
| `defaults.cache.ttl_seconds` | unset | Provider cache time to live. (seconds, 1 or more). |
| `defaults.cache.min_prefix` | unset | Smallest prefix the provider caches. (tokens, 1 or more). |
| `defaults.cache.context_window` | per model | Context window size; read-heavy preference needs at least 1000000. (tokens, 1 or more). |
| `defaults.cache.read_heavy_weight` | 3 | Weight multiplier for read-heavy and review work on cheap-cache models. (1 to 255). |
| `defaults.compaction.window` | per model | Context size at which compaction is advised. (tokens, 1 or more). |
| `defaults.compaction.mode` | per model | When compaction is advised. (auto, task_boundary or never). |
| `defaults.compaction.min_turns` | per model | Fewest turns before compaction is advised. (turns, 1 or more). |
| `defaults.lane.max_context` | unset | Enforced largest context for a lane on this model. (tokens, 1 or more). |
| `defaults.lane.max_turns` | unset | Enforced most turns for a lane on this model. (turns, 1 or more). |
| `defaults.lane.stop_early_ok` | false | false asks writers to report completion through the shared handoff. (true or false). |
| `defaults.lane.max_continuations` | 2 | Maximum automatic writer continuations after a stopped_early handoff; 0 disables continuation. (0 to 8). |
| `defaults.lane.resume_continuations` | false | Resume the retained provider session for automatic writer continuations when available; otherwise start a fresh attempt on the same worktree with the handoff and original brief. Overridable per model and project. (bool). |
| `defaults.lane.user_skills` | inherit domains.lanes.user_skills | Override host and project user skill discovery for matching routes. rules.policy.lane.user_skills uses the same values. (discover or off). |
| `defaults.lane.read_only` | per model | true refuses write lanes on this model. (true or false). |
| `defaults.result.check` | per model | Check the result for the required sections before accepting it. (true or false). |
| `defaults.result.sections` | per model | Heading lines a result must contain. (exact section heading lines; empty clears). |
| `defaults.result.fallback` | per model | Model for the one fallback attempt when the result check fails. (model id). |
| `defaults.result.fallback_effort` | per model | Effort for the fallback attempt. (effort name). |
| `rules` | empty | Layered overrides ordered by scope: global, adapter, model, account, model plus account; later rules win at equal scope. Schedule start is inclusive, expiry and window end are exclusive; an overnight window wraps midnight; inactive rules have no effect. (tables with adapter, model, account, schedule {starts, expires as RFC 3339 timestamps, windows [{weekdays?, start_hour, end_hour}] in UTC} and policy (the same fields as defaults, under rules.policy); weekdays use Monday-based indexes, Monday 0 through Sunday 6). |

## Quota history and plan prices

Set the cap in `[domains.quota]`; set prices per account as shown.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `history_max_bytes` | 4194304 (4 MiB) | Disk cap for each account's quota history under quota/history/. Readings go to a current file that rotates to one predecessor at half the cap, so the pair never exceeds it and the newest reading is always kept. (65536 to 134217728 bytes). |

### Account plan prices

```json
{
  "effect": "Prices over time for the account. The entry with the latest effective_from on or before a reading applies to it, and quota history --json shows it as plan_price, with price and notional_usd. Dates must differ within an account; unknown keys, negative or non-finite prices and bad dates refuse the config. This is not the detected plan label, which comes from the provider or the account's plan option.",
  "fields": {
    "currency": "Three capital letters (ISO 4217). USD when omitted. No conversion is applied.",
    "effective_from": "First day the price applies, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC).",
    "name": "Plan label, for example max_5x. At most 64 characters.",
    "notional_usd": "Optional list-price value in USD of a free or discounted plan, for example 20 for a student plan priced 0.",
    "price": "Price per month in currency; 0 or more, 0 for a free plan."
  },
  "form": "array of tables, any number of entries",
  "path": "domains.accounts.entries.<id>.plans"
}
```

## Provider updates

```json
{
  "path": "providers.<id>",
  "provider_ids": [
    "claude",
    "codex",
    "cursor",
    "agy",
    "opencode"
  ],
  "runtime_deadline_seconds": {
    "default": "unset",
    "effect": "Cap on the wall-clock runtime of any lane on this provider. A dispatch's own --provider-timeout applies when it is shorter. At the deadline the provider is stopped and the attempt settles as timed_out, whatever the host did meanwhile, including sleeping.",
    "max": 14400,
    "min": 1,
    "type": "int"
  },
  "update": {
    "default": true,
    "effect": "Run the detected native updater in a detached one-shot worker scheduled by quota events. Provider preparation briefly shares the update lock; running lanes do not hold it. If all candidates are updating, dispatch waits at most --wait (capped at 30 seconds), then uses the installed version. false opts out; {command: [program, argument, ...]} overrides the updater directly without a shell.",
    "type": "bool_or_command_argv"
  },
  "update_interval_seconds": {
    "default": 86400,
    "effect": "Minimum time between update attempts, checked on existing housekeeping events. Failed and interrupted attempts and result-write errors wait the same interval.",
    "min": 1,
    "type": "int"
  },
  "update_timeout_seconds": {
    "default": 300,
    "effect": "Maximum native updater duration in the detached worker. Timeout kills the updater process group and records failure. Updater descendants retain the exclusive lease until exit, including descendants that leave the group.",
    "min": 1,
    "type": "int"
  }
}
```

## `lanes.context_handoff_tokens`

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `default` | `0` |
| `effect` | `"Context size, in tokens one provider call sent, at which the host stops a writer so a fresh attempt continues from its handoff on the same worktree. The stop settles as a declared stop and uses the graph's one automatic continuation; commits and uncommitted edits stay in place. 0 is off. Suggested setting 200000. Only providers that report each call's context (Claude) are stopped; others keep today's behaviour."` |
| `max` | `2000000` |
| `min` | `0` |
| `reader` | `"tools/front-door/crates/run/src/launch.rs, tools/front-door/crates/supervisor/src/guardian.rs"` |
| `status` | `"wired"` |
| `trade_off` | `"Lower stops paying for very large contexts sooner but restarts more often, and a restart may lose working state that the handoff does not record; off until a trial shows restart does not lower completion."` |

| `default` | `"all"` |

Set per run with --knob lanes.local_cargo=check, per graph node with &#96;attempt.local_cargo&#96;, or for the host under [knobs]."` |

|---|---|
| `default` | `"standard"` |
| `effect` | `"minimal marks a silent provider only after the longest silence interval (one hour) instead of lanes.silence_seconds. Set per graph node with &#96;attempt.supervision&#96; or the &#96;light&#96; preset."` |
| `reader` | `"tools/front-door/crates/run/src/launch.rs"` |
| `status` | `"wired"` |
| `trade_off` | `"minimal reports a stalled lane later; deadlines, custody and confinement are unchanged."` |
| `type` | `"enum"` |
| `values` | `["standard", "minimal"]` |

## `routing.allow_unknown_partial_headroom`

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `default` | `false` |
| `effect` | `"Allow uncalibrated partial quota headroom below the limit."` |
| `host_only` | `true` |
| `reader` | `"tools/front-door/crates/cli/src/route.rs"` |
| `status` | `"wired"` |
| `strict` | `true` |
| `trade_off` | `"Partial coverage cannot prove remaining allowance; exhausted lower bounds still block selection."` |
| `type` | `"bool"` |

## `routing.exclude`

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `default` | `[]` |
| `effect` | `"Keep each listed provider (claude), account (label, entry or adapter/key) or exact model (adapter/id) out of named-route pools for every task. A standing list; &#96;--exclude&#96; and a graph's list are added to it, not substituted for it. A pinned &#96;--model&#96; is never affected."` |
| `reader` | `"tools/front-door/crates/cli/src/route.rs"` |
| `status` | `"wired"` |
| `strict` | `true` |
| `trade_off` | `"Selection still weighs pacing and readiness over the remaining members, but an exclusion that empties a pool refuses the dispatch rather than widening it."` |
| `type` | `"string_list"` |

## `routing.flag_exclude`

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `default` | `[]` |
| `effect` | `"The exclusion list one dispatch carries, set by advanced route resolution. Same selectors as &#96;routing.exclude&#96;; refusals and &#96;--explain&#96; name the flag as the source."` |
| `reader` | `"tools/front-door/crates/cli/src/route.rs"` |
| `status` | `"wired"` |
| `strict` | `true` |
| `trade_off` | `"Applies to this dispatch only; the standing &#96;routing.exclude&#96; list and a graph's list still apply."` |
| `type` | `"string_list"` |

## `routing.graph_exclude`

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `default` | `[]` |
| `effect` | `"The exclusion list a graph passes to each node it launches, set from graph routing policy. Same selectors as &#96;routing.exclude&#96;; refusals and &#96;--explain&#96; name the graph as the source."` |
| `reader` | `"tools/front-door/crates/cli/src/route.rs"` |
| `status` | `"wired"` |
| `strict` | `true` |
| `trade_off` | `"Applies to every node's named-route pool; a node's pinned model is never affected."` |
| `type` | `"string_list"` |

## `routing.workload`

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `default` | `"general"` |
| `effect` | `"Describe the task for model policy. Read-heavy and review work give cheap-cache, million-token models a configurable preference in pools."` |
| `reader` | `"tools/front-door/crates/cli/src/run.rs"` |
| `status` | `"wired"` |
| `trade_off` | `"A preference preserves model choice and readiness gates; it does not force every read-heavy task onto one model."` |
| `type` | `"enum"` |
| `values` | `["general", "read_heavy", "edit_heavy", "review"]` |

## `usage.project_attribution`

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `default` | `false` |
| `effect` | `"Include the existing project identifier in local usage events."` |

{
  "presets": {
    "balanced": {
      "description": "Today's behaviour: every knob at its registry default.",
      "knobs": {}
    },
    "economy": {
      "description": "Lower lane concurrency, accepting slower runs.",
      "knobs": {
        "lanes.max_concurrency": 4,
        "lanes.max_concurrency_read_only": 8
